job_title: Data Center Facility Engineer, Data Center Engineering Operations
job_description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation
of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the
cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage,
networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have
continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging
problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re
looking for talented people who want to help.
Key job responsibilities
• Install, maintain, and repair pipework, fittings, valves, and manifolds across
cooling distribution loops, chilled water systems, and condenser water circuits
• Operate and maintain air handling units (AHUs), chillers, cooling towers,
evaporative cooling systems, and liquid cooling infrastructure
• Perform pressure testing, leak detection, and system integrity checks on
pressurised water circuits
• Manage water treatment programmes in line with ACOP L8 and HSG274
requirements, including legionella risk assessments, temperature monitoring,
chemical dosing, and biocide application
• Maintain and troubleshoot pumps, heat exchangers, coolant distribution units
(CDUs), and associated mechanical components
• Monitor thermal performance of cooling systems and identify opportunities to
optimise flow rates, delta-T, and energy efficiency
• Support commissioning and decommissioning of mechanical cooling infrastructure
during capacity additions

changes, belt replacements, pump seal replacements, bearing inspections, and
valve servicing
• Respond to alarms and incidents related to leaks, pressure anomalies, thermal
exceedances, or water quality deviations within SLA
• Maintain accurate records of maintenance activities, water treatment logs,
system parameters, and defect logs
• Collaborate with controls engineers on BMS/SCADA integration for mechanical
plant monitoring
• Adhere to all site safety procedures including permit-to-work, LOTO, and
working at height protocols
• Work safely at all times, following risk assessments, method statements, and
safe systems of work (SSOW) for all maintenance and operational activities
• Support continuous improvement initiatives to enhance system reliability and
reduce mean time to repair
A day in the life
Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred
qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates
to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path,
or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.
Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted
cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating —
that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies
trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led
affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our
differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our
Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity)
conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and
other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded
professional.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the
expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of
our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home,
there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.
About the team
Amazon Web Services Data Center Engineering Operations (DCEO) is seeking a
mechanically-biased Engineering Operations Technician to join our team. This
hands-on role is focused on the installation, maintenance, and troubleshooting
of mechanical cooling and water systems infrastructure across our data centre
portfolio. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas
and empowers you to own them to completion. (AIS tagline)
You will work directly with air handling units, chillers, cooling towers,
evaporative cooling systems, liquid cooling distribution, and associated water
treatment plant. The role demands strong mechanical aptitude with specific
expertise in plumbing, pipework, pressurised water systems, and fluid dynamics.
You will be responsible for maintaining system integrity, ensuring compliance
with ACOP regulations, optimising thermal performance, and supporting the
scaling of cooling capacity as our fleet grows.
This is a shift-based role requiring flexibility to support 24/7 data centre
operations. You will work alongside electrical and controls engineers but your
primary focus is mechanical systems and fluid management.
Basic Qualifications: - Knowledge of mechanical systems (Mechanical, HVAC
systems, Controls)
- Experience reading and writing procedures, technical documents, and
engineering drawings
- Knowledge of generic mechanical room infrastructure such as chillers, cooler
units, and fan controls
- NVQ Level 3 in Mechanical, Electrical or Mechatronics, or NFQ Level 3 (or
equivalent) in Mechanical, Electrical or Mechatronics
- Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or
holidays
- Demonstrable experience working with pressurised water systems, pipework
installations, and fluid distribution networks
- Knowledge of ACOP L8 (Legionnaires' disease: The control of legionella
bacteria in water systems) and HSG274 guidance, with experience implementing
compliant water treatment regimes
- Practical understanding of fluid dynamics principles including flow rates,
pressure drop, cavitation, and heat transfer Preferred Qualifications: -
Experience with EPMS/SCADA/BMS controls system software or hardware
- Direct experience with liquid cooling technologies such as CDUs, rear-door
heat exchangers, or direct-to-chip cooling
- City & Guilds 2079 or equivalent Legionella control qualification
- Knowledge of water treatment processes including closed-loop and open-loop
system management, corrosion inhibitors, and microbiological control
- IOSH Managing Safely or NEBOSH General Certificate
- Experience with commissioning or decommissioning of mechanical systems
- Understanding of cooling architectures and thermal management principles

from greenlight through final cost close-out. You'll define how we measure,
report, and communicate financial performance across UK productions, owning the

relies on to surface risks early, explain variances clearly, and keep financial

for production finance across the EU organisation.
Amazon MGM Studios is one of the UK's largest investors in film and television
production, with a permanent production home at Bray Film Studios and a
long-term presence at Shepperton Studios. Our UK-produced originals span
scripted drama, feature films, and tentpole series reaching hundreds of millions
of Prime Video customers globally. We operate with a start-up mentality inside a
global organisation - small, collaborative teams that move quickly, take
ownership, and solve complex problems at scale.
At Amazon, we believe that in-person collaboration is essential to our culture
and innovation. While we allow flexibility for personal circumstances, we
generally expect employees to work from our offices five days a week. This
approach has consistently shown that spontaneous interactions, rapid
problem-solving, and the energy of in-person teamwork lead to better results for
our customers. In particular, our data shows that teams working together in
person are more effective at making complex decisions, onboarding new team
members, and fostering the kind of creative collaboration that has driven
Amazon's success. The serendipitous hallway conversations and impromptu
whiteboarding sessions that happen naturally in an office environment have
proven invaluable to our invention process and maintaining our high bar for
excellence.
Key job responsibilities
- Lead Production Finance operations for Amazon Studios film and television
projects in the UK, independently managing all stages of the production
lifecycle.
- Define and own the production finance metrics and reporting strategy -
executive dashboards, management reporting, and operational KPIs.
- Serve as financial controller for UK productions - ensuring controllership
oversight, error-free reporting, and proactive compliance risk resolution.
- Oversee production funding in multiple currencies, managing cash disbursement
controls to support production activities and mitigate financial risk.
- Build and maintain excellent working relationships with external production
companies, finance partners and public bodies.
- Drive month-end close (cash flow, costs, accruals); identify variances,
articulate root causes, and communicate findings to leadership.
- Collaborate cross-functionally with Creative, Business Affairs, Legal,
Accounting, and Production to execute payments and resolve financial issues.
- Invent and simplify - improve, scale, or automate processes and tools across
teams, setting standards that others can follow. Basic Qualifications: -
Bachelor's degree in BI, finance, engineering, statistics, computer science,
mathematics, finance or equivalent quantitative field, or Professional
accounting qualification (e.g. ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CPA, or equivalent)
- Progressive experience in Production/Finance/Accounting or Business Accounting
with some exposure to the Film and Television Production Industry.
- Knowledge of local tax incentives and regional funding schemes.
- Experience that includes strong analytical skills, use of AI tools, attention
to detail, and effective communication abilities, or experience with automation
and any version control tools Preferred Qualifications: - Familiarity with UK/US
union and guild agreements (Bectu/PACT, residuals, guild compliance)
- Understanding of content financing models (pre-sales, gap financing, equity,
tax-based structures) and the end-to-end value chain of film and television -

# Sales Development Performance Lead
Brighton, East Sussex, United Kingdom
### What You'll Do
Want to kick off an exciting career with a fast-growing cloud technology business in a complicated, exciting & high growth area of regulatory compliance? We are looking for a Director Inside Sales to join our Leadership team to make an outstanding contribution to the growth of our EMEA business.
Reporting to the VP of Sales Development, you will oversee a sales development organization, providing strategic direction, leadership, coaching and mentoring. Using your leadership skills, you will inspire this group of frontline Sales Development Representatives (both Inbound and Outbound) and lead the way for the development of future talent in an exciting, innovative, and growing SaaS company!
Your team consists of bold, competitive and diverse individuals across multiple European geographies, who will identify new prospects and high value opportunities through inbound & outbound prospecting methods.
### What Your Responsibilities Will Be
* Execute on the demand generation plans to support the company's strategic growth goals
* Support the evolution of the business development function incorporating AI technologies and automation into sales development workflows
* Understand the changing needs of the business and ensure the development of new talent is aligned to support these needs
* Lead the EMEA based Sales Development team and have dotted line responsibility for the Pune team that supports EMEA to ensure global best practices and SOPs are followed and enforced – partner with the Pune based EMEA leader to orchestrate alignment across this function with revenue marketing, growth marketing, and sales
* Leverage data to derive trends, inform next practices and improve overall process and execution across teams
* Motivate them to exceed objectives through coaching, weekly one on ones, daily metric tracking and creative incentives
* Help create a fun, high energy environment where people love coming to work
* Oversee and monitor the effective use of Salesforce and other CRM tools
* Work closely with senior management team to refine process, talk tracks and update training documentation
* As the regional leader, ensure positive and collaborative working relationships with both the marketing and sales organizations to maximize the sales representatives' impact
* Compile daily and weekly reports for quality assurance
### What You’ll Need To Be Successful
* Degree educated or equivalent in a business management related topic.
* Successful sales career with a minimum of 10 years+
* A love of cold calling and a willingness to jump on the phones and demonstrate ‘what success looks like’ for your team members
* A strong background of AI use and an understanding of how automation can be leveraged to enable and empower sales development reps – a desire to test and learn
* A minimum of 3 years+ proven experience leading through people leaders in sales management for telephone-based sales, business development or SDR teams preferably in SaaS or technology sales
* Proven skill set of identifying great talent and scaling a successful geographical dispersed business development organization
* A strategic thinker with the ability to adapt and deliver consistent growth during times of business transformation
* A desire to be a hands-on and engaged leader who loves the energy of and wants to be in the ‘Pit’
### Avalara is an AI-first Company
AI is embedded in our workflows, decision-making, and products. Success here requires embracing AI as an essential capability.
* You’ll bring experience using AI and AI-related technologies, ready to thrive here.
* You’ll apply AI every day to business challenges - improving efficiency, contributing solutions, and driving results for your team, our company, and our customers.
* You’ll grow with AI by staying curious about new trends and best practices, and by sharing what you learn so others can benefit too.

Total Rewards In addition to a great compensation package, paid time off, and paid parental leave, many Avalara employees are eligible for bonuses. Inclusive culture and diversity Avalara strongly supports diversity, equity, and inclusion, and is committed to integrating them into our business practices and our organizational culture. Our growth is real - we're a billion dollar business - and we’re not slowing down until we’ve achieved our mission - to be part of every transaction in the world.

# SAP Basis Automation Engineer
Avantra is the leading observability and automation platform for SAP operations, built to give enterprises and managed service providers control, visibility, and automation across hybrid SAP landscapes. We help SAP teams run faster, safer, and smarter, on ECC, S/4HANA, RISE, BTP and SaaS.
As we continue to grow, we are expanding our SAP Engineering team with a new SAP Basis Automation Engineer. SAP Engineering at Avantra is mostly about engineering; analysing and developing solutions that are shipped on our platform, but we also play a key part in the product; identifying the problems we can solve and guiding the development of our platform.
The person we are looking for has strong experience in running SAP software for multiple customers. They will have strong SAP Basis experience, and must use automation and scripting to achieve their goals, whilst still having dreams of what else they wish they could build to help them in their role.
## **Responsibilities**
* Analyse SAP software on-premises and in the cloud to design and specify new automations and solve observability problems
* Develop automations to solve SAP operations problems, including scripting and development, testing, documentation and shipping the software
* Provide a strong product opinion for what problem we solve next, how we solve it, and what you would want if you were using Avantra to run SAP landscapes
* Install, configure and maintain SAP software to replicate real-life cutting-edge scenarios and support the continued development of Avantra
* Stay up-to-date and knowledgeable about the latest SAP technologies and developments, best practices and cybersecurity as well as SAP-adjacent technologies
## **What You Bring**
* More than five years of experience in running and supporting SAP landscapes
* Deep SAP Basis expertise, ideally gained in a service provider environment or across multiple SAP customers with hands-on work and decision making
* Programming, scripting or low-code automation experience (e.g. JavaScript, Python, PowerShell, Avantra automations, or Ansible) and knowledge of Linux
* Exposure to SAP cloud technologies (eg. SAP Business Technology Platform, RISE with SAP, SAP Core AI, Joule, or Clean Core projects)
* Experience with technical security and compliance in SAP, perhaps from answering auditors requests or working in a regulated environment
* Hands-on experience with observability, automation or security tools like SAP Solution Manager, SAP Cloud ALM, or those from third-parties
* Excellent communication skills to explain complex security issues to both engineers and executives
#### About Avantra
Avantra is a high growth tech company with 26 years of Swiss precision engineering coupled with the energy of a start-up. Our product is the leading AIOps platform for SAP operations, enabling customers to achieve hyperautomation success. Our customers are large multinational enterprises and household names, including national and global managed service providers. We have teams based across Switzerland, Germany, UK, US and Eastern Europe.
Our culture is something we are incredibly proud of and strive to protect. We live our values of Be Caring, Embrace Challenge and Stay Curious every day through company mindfulness sessions, wellbeing days and retaining a family feel. If this sounds like a good fit for you, why not say hello?

# Senior DevOps Engineer
**Role:** Senior DevOps Engineer
**Salary:** £70,000 - 90,000 DOE
**Location:** Southampton (hybrid - min 3 days per week on site)
We are looking for a Senior DevOps Engineer to help us design and deliver our platform architecture on Microsoft Azure. You will bring deep, hands-on expertise in cloud-native infrastructure, secure deployment practices, container orchestration, big data workloads and cost optimisation, and you will apply that expertise to build systems capable of operating reliably at global scale.
**Senior DevOps Engineer,** the role:
*Architecture & Platform Design*
* Design the target-state platform architecture on Microsoft Azure, selecting appropriate modern Azure services and reference patterns for a large-scale, globally distributed software estate.
* Architect scalable, resilient and secure infrastructure using Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) and Platform as a Service (PaaS) offerings, choosing the right model for each workload.
* Design content delivery and edge strategy using Azure Front Door and Azure CDN to deliver low-latency performance to a global user base.
* Own the container orchestration strategy across Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), Azure Container Apps and serverless container options, and advise on where a service mesh (for example Istio or Linkerd) adds value.
* Design and support large-scale data platform infrastructure, supporting the ingestion, storage, processing and querying of high-volume datasets using Azure data services such as Data Lake Storage, Databricks, Synapse Analytics and Event Hubs.
* Document architecture decisions, trade-offs and standards so that they are transparent, repeatable and understood across the engineering teams.
*Secure Deployment & DevSecOps*
* Embed security best practice into every layer of the platform, applying a defence-in-depth and zero-trust approach appropriate to a business handling sensitive financial and tax data.
* Implement secure-by-design deployment pipelines, including secrets management (Azure Key Vault), identity and access management (Microsoft Entra ID), network segmentation and least-privilege access controls.
* Integrate security scanning, policy-as-code and compliance guardrails into the delivery lifecycle using tools such as Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Azure Policy.
* Work with the IT and security functions to ensure infrastructure meets internal governance, data protection and regulatory requirements.
*Automation, CI/CD & Infrastructure as Code*
* Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions to enable fast, safe and repeatable deployments.
* Define all infrastructure as code using Terraform and Bicep, promoting modular, reusable and version-controlled definitions.
* Champion GitOps ways of working and automate provisioning, configuration and release management to reduce manual effort and human error.
* Implement deployment strategies such as blue/green and canary releases to minimise risk and downtime.
*Reliability, Observability & Cost Optimisation*
* Establish observability across the platform, including monitoring, logging, tracing and alerting (for example Azure Monitor, Application Insights and Log Analytics).
* Drive reliability engineering practices, defining service level objectives and improving resilience, scalability and disaster recovery posture.
* Lead on cloud cost optimisation (FinOps), continuously reviewing spend, right-sizing resources and building cost awareness into architecture and delivery decisions.
* Respond to incidents, lead root-cause analysis and drive continuous improvement of the platform.
*Collaboration & Leadership*
* Act as a technical authority on DevOps and cloud architecture across both the IT and Software Engineering departments.
* Mentor and upskill software engineers on secure deployment, automation and cloud-native practices.
* Partner closely with the Group IT Director to align the platform roadmap with wider business and technology strategy.
* Contribute to a strong engineering culture built on quality, security, automation and shared ownership.
**Senior DevOps Engineer,** the person:
*Essential Skills & Experience*
* Experience: 5 to 8 years of hands-on experience in DevOps, platform or cloud engineering, including production ownership of business-critical systems.
* Azure: Deep, demonstrable expertise with Microsoft Azure, including core compute, networking, storage, identity and security services.
* Kubernetes: Proven experience designing and running workloads on Kubernetes (AKS) at scale, including containerisation with Docker.
* IaC: Strong hands-on experience with both Terraform and Bicep for infrastructure as code.
* CI/CD: Practical experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines with GitHub Actions.
* Security: Solid understanding of secure deployment, identity and access management, secrets management and network security in the cloud.
* Scale: Experience designing for global scale, including CDN, edge delivery, high availability and disaster recovery.
* Cost: Demonstrable experience of cloud cost optimisation and FinOps practices.
* Big Data: Hands-on experience building or operating infrastructure for big data and high-volume data workloads, including distributed processing, data pipelines and scalable storage.
* Automation: Strong scripting ability (for example PowerShell, Bash or Python) for automation.
* Certification: A current, valid Microsoft Azure certification (for example AZ-400 Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions, or an Azure Administrator/Solutions Architect credential).
* Communication: Ability to communicate architecture and trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
*Desirable Skills & Experience*
* Microsoft Azure Solutions Architect Expert or a security-focused certification such as Azure Security Engineer Associate or CISSP.
* Experience with service mesh technologies (Istio, Linkerd) and advanced networking.
* Experience in a regulated, financial services or compliance-driven environment.
* Familiarity with observability tooling such as Prometheus, Grafana or Datadog.
* Experience with big data technologies and frameworks such as Azure Databricks, Synapse Analytics, Apache Spark, Kafka or Data Lake architectures.
* Experience supporting multi-entity, multi-jurisdiction or globally distributed operations.
* Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) or equivalent
**Senior DevOps Engineer,** the benefits:
* 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays.
* Annual leave purchase scheme (up to 5 days per year).
* Company Pension scheme (Royal London).
* Cycle2Work Scheme.
* Private Healthcare Insurance (Vitality).
* Flexible working.
* Regular departmental socials, company wide.

AVASK assist hundreds of Amazon FBA sellers as well as entrepreneurs across eBay, Shopify and many other platforms. Providing clients with a comprehensive range of expertise - from practical guidance on cross-border transactions, to ensuring they are fully compliant.

* You’ll provide commercial leadership across Financial Services, owning proposals, statements of work, delivery commercials and team shaping, while working with industry teams to originate, qualify and build a strong pipeline of DAISE opportunities
* You’ll act as the day-to-day interlock between DAISE and Financial Services teams, connecting sector ambition with DAISE capability and shaping expertise in both directions. You’ll help embed data, analytics and AI thinking into sector priorities, propositions and client conversations, while bringing market insight, client needs and delivery learnings back into DAISE to strengthen our services, assets and future propositions.
* You’ll build trusted relationships with senior clients across Financial Services and within Baringa, raising DAISE’s profile through sector conversations, client engagement, client events and industry conferences, and shaping data and AI opportunities that respond to market priorities and create measurable client value.

**SUMMARY**
The Sterility Assurance specialist provides technical expertise and support to the UK and Ireland Compounding Sites for all sterility assurance aspects. Acts as a valuable and effective source of information and advice on sterility assurance and positively contributes to the network Quality Management Team. Responsible for ensuring that the UK and Ireland Compounding Sites maintain a robust, effective and compliant sterility assurance and environmental control and monitoring process in conjunction with the global strategy.
**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**
* Responsible for ensuring effective Sterility Assurance and Environmental Monitoring programmes are deployed in UK and Ireland Compounding facilities, in compliance with current GMP and Baxter global strategy.
* Provide technical support and guidance on Sterility Assurance, Environmental Monitoring, environmental control, Contamination Control Strategy and aseptic practices across UK and Ireland Compounding facilities.
* Support risk management activities relating to Sterility Assurance, Environmental Monitoring, Contamination Control Strategy and aseptic practices, including support of site RTRA processes as required.
* Support the Global Compounding organization on standardisation of Sterility Assurance practices and identification and implementation of new technology for microbiological testing and environmental control
* Participation in continuous improvement projects and providing the expert guidance and assessment for the questions related with Sterility Assurance, including risk reduction initiatives in line with company strategy
* Provide coaching, mentoring and technical guidance to operational and quality teams in relation to Sterility Assurance, Environmental Monitoring, environmental control and aseptic practices.
* Provide technical oversight and interpretation of validation, qualification or study data related to Sterility Assurance, Environmental Monitoring, environmental control and aseptic practices, as required.
* Support inspection readiness and participate in internal, corporate and regulatory audits as the technical representative for Sterility Assurance, Environmental Monitoring, environmental control and aseptic practices, as required.
* Review and assess Environmental Monitoring reports and protocols to ensure compliance with regulatory standards and internationally acceptable standards.
* Support and lead problem solving investigations for product and process deviations or customer complaints.
* Participate in complaint investigation, non-conformance and quality incidents investigation, act as technical approver where required.
* Provide technical input to change controls where Sterility Assurance, Environmental Monitoring, Contamination Control Strategy, environmental control or aseptic practices may be impacted
* Provide technical support in the interpretation of microbial identification and Environmental Monitoring data, including trending of EM and microbiological data and setting of appropriate Alert limits
* Support Environmental Monitoring Management Software approval, configuration and reporting.
* Responsible for the tracking and reporting of Quality Metrics for internal and external use.
* Support the development and review of of quality documentation including local SOPs and documents related to Sterility Assurance, Environmental Monitoring, Contamination Control Strategy and aseptic practices, acting as document owner or Technical Approver as required.
* Provide microbiological expertise, training and operational guidance to operational and quality staff on Sterility Assurance, Environmental Monitoring, environmental control and aseptic practices, including periodic reassessment as required.
* Identify new, or changes to existing, processes and systems to improve effectiveness and efficiency of the Sterility Assurance programme whilst maintaining compliance with Corporate and Regulatory requirements.
* Adhere to Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) policies, procedures and requirements.
* Support maintenance of a safe place to work through escalation of unsafe EHS practices
* Maintain professional status and standards
* Fully support the Quality Policy and business goals and objectives by building quality into all aspects of work.
* Any other tasks from Sterility Assurance Manager.

* **Preferred** 5 years’ experience of microbiology experience in an aseptic facility
* Strong operational experience preferably in an aseptic manufacturing background
* Experience of aseptic technique
* Excellent interpersonal skills
* Passionate advocate of quality as a discipline and continuous improvement
* Have experience in the use of quality improvement and problem solving skills (ie FMEA, DMAIC, Process Mapping etc) and the interpretation of data, experience of Lean manufacturing

## **WE ARE BBC STUDIOWORKS**
BBC Studioworks is a commercial subsidiary of BBC Studios providing studios and post production services to all the major TV broadcasters and production companies including the BBC, ITV, Sky, Channel 4, Channel 5, Amazon & Netflix. Located across sites in Elstree and Television Centre in White City, our London facilities are home to some of the nation’s most watched and loved television shows. We offer world-class studio and post production spaces, equip them with the right technology and engage the most dedicated and talented people in the industry. By doing this, we bring shows to life. We have 3 studios at BBC TV Centre one of which is 4K UHD capable. Elstree having 3 dedicated studios for our commercial work and an additional 9 shooting areas and 4 galleries to film the continuing Drama Eastenders. Studioworks also have a studio in Glasgow at Kelvin Hall and also at Digbeth Loc Studios in Birmingham.
**PURPOSE OF THE ROLE** As a Studio Engineer, you will play a key role in ensuring the technical readiness and reliability of broadcast facilities across Television Centre. Working across multiple studios and production environments, you will maintain, align, modify and operate a wide range of broadcast systems and equipment. You will provide expert technical support to production teams, troubleshoot complex issues, and help develop innovative solutions that enable the successful delivery of world-class television..
**WHY JOIN THE TEAM** This is an opportunity to work at the heart of a fast-paced, high-profile production environment where no two days are the same. You'll collaborate closely with production teams, anticipate their needs and contribute to the delivery of world-class television. The role offers exposure to diverse technologies and systems, opportunities to solve complex technical challenges, and the chance to develop your skills while supporting a flagship BBC programme.
**YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT:**
* Maintain, align, modify and troubleshoot broadcast equipment and systems, ensuring technical facilities meet operational, production and engineering standards.
* Partner with production teams and resource departments to understand requirements, provide technical expertise, attend planning meetings and deliver effective broadcast solutions.
* Identify, diagnose and resolve technical faults, implementing alternative solutions where required to minimise disruption and studio downtime.
* Drive technical innovation through the development, modification and testing of equipment, systems and workflows to meet evolving production needs.
* Rig, configure and operate studio equipment including EVS record servers, vision monitoring systems, camera shading/colour balance controls and associated broadcast infrastructure.
* Lead or support refurbishment projects and complex engineering activities, working with BBC specialist teams, contractors and manufacturers to implement technical improvements and resolve design issues.
* Promote a safe and efficient working environment by ensuring compliance with health and safety requirements, maintaining accurate records and reports, addressing facility issues, and providing training, guidance and supervision to junior staff, trainees and work experience placements.
## YOUR SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE
**ESSENTIAL CRITERIA:**
* Relevant qualifications, training, or significant practical experience in broadcast engineering within a television studio, live production or broadcast environment.
* Strong technical knowledge of broadcast technology, including cameras, routers, vision and audio mixers, sound desks, communications systems, talkback infrastructure, computer systems and networks.
* Experience working with a range of broadcast systems and software, with the ability to quickly learn and adapt to new technologies and workflows.
* Ability to maintain high technical standards, including the critical assessment of television pictures, waveforms, audio quality and overall signal performance.
* Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with a customer-focused approach and the ability to build effective relationships with production, operational and engineering teams.
* Proven problem-solving and decision-making skills, with the ability to prioritise competing demands, identify practical solutions, and know when to escalate, refer or delegate issues appropriately.
* A highly self-motivated and collaborative team player with a positive, flexible approach and a strong understanding of production requirements. Able to perform the essential audio and visual quality assessment requirements of the role - Please note: This role involves critical assessment of audio and visual content, including colour accuracy and sound quality, as part of studio engineering responsibilities.

If you want to work at the intersection of AI and governance, on problems that matter at the highest level, this is a strong place to be.
Our Mission
We unleash the potential of organisations through the science of board effectiveness, building better businesses and benefitting society.
**The Role**
You own CRM and email as a performance channel. That means the sends, the segments, the data underneath them, and the decisions about what goes to whom and when.
You will build, QA and send emails across HubSpot and Planhat, own database quality, own the cross channel send calendar, and report on how the channel performs. You will generate and test your own copy variants using AI rather than waiting on someone else. You will work closely with Sales, Customer Success and our GTM Engineer so that outbound sequences and marketing communications complement each other instead of competing for the same inbox.
This is a role for someone early in their marketing career who wants to own a channel rather than support one.
**Main Responsibilities**
* Build, QA, schedule and send emails across HubSpot and Planhat, generating and testing your own copy variants against segment behaviour
* Own database hygiene, enrichment and list building, automating the repeatable parts
* Own the cross channel send calendar. You decide how much we send and when, and you protect the contact experience
* Own engagement health across the database, including re-engagement decisions, flow design, and measuring whether flows still work over time
* Report on CRM as a performance channel: deliverability, opens, clicks, conversions, and what to do differently next month
* Ensure leads entering the CRM are compliant, enriched, correctly tracked, and triggering the right downstream actions, including opportunity creation
* Work with Sales and Customer Success so outbound sequences, including Gong Engage, complement marketing communications rather than clash with them
* Work with the GTM Engineer on CRM integrations, lead scoring models, and data flows
* Flag and escalate site issues that affect campaign performance, including page speed and broken journeys
**Person Specification**
This role suits someone at the start of their marketing career who is already AI native in how they work, comfortable with data, and exacting about detail. We are open to candidates with one to three years in a CRM, lifecycle or email marketing role, ideally in B2B SaaS, and equally open to strong early career candidates with no marketing experience who can evidence the qualities below. HubSpot, Planhat and HTML can all be taught to the right person.
Campaign strategy and creative concepting sit elsewhere in the team. This role owns the channel, the data, and the decisions about how we reach people.

* You have established a send calendar and a contact frequency standard that Sales, Customer Success and Marketing all work to

## The Role
We’re looking for a Senior Embedded Systems Engineer to help own the firmware and embedded systems at the heart of Carv.
This is a firmware-leaning role for someone who is comfortable working across the full hardware stack. You should be strong at embedded software, but also confident reading schematics, bringing up boards, debugging electronics in the lab, and working with production test systems.
You do not need to be a pure PCB layout specialist. You do need to be the kind of engineer who can debug issues across electronics and firmware.
You’ll work on next-generation sensor development, production firmware, automated test equipment and internal diagnostic tools used by over 100,000 skiers globally.
## What You'll Do
* Architect, develop, and maintain firmware for Carv’s connected sensor systems.
* Work on low-power, resource-constrained embedded systems using embedded C/C++.
* Help develop next-generation sensing hardware, including early prototypes, bring-up, validation, and productionisation.
* Debug issues across firmware, electronics, Bluetooth, sensors, power, and manufacturing test systems.
* Build and improve production firmware, test jigs, automated test equipment, and calibration or diagnostic workflows.
* Work with manufacturing partners to improve reliability, yield, and production debug tooling.
* Develop internal tools that help our team and Customer Success proactively diagnose hardware and firmware issues in the field.
* Collaborate closely within the hardware team and with the data science, app, and product teams.
* Mentor other engineers and raise the standard for how we design, test, document, and debug embedded systems.
## What We're Looking For
* 7+ years of experience in embedded systems, firmware, or closely related hardware product development.
* Strong embedded C/C++ experience on resource-constrained devices.
* Strong bare metal and RTOS experience (Zephyr preferred).
* Experience taking firmware or embedded systems from prototype through to production (10k+ unit volume).
* Comfortable debugging hardware with tools such as oscilloscopes, logic analysers, debuggers, and RF/Bluetooth diagnostic tools.
* Ability to read schematics and reason about electronics, sensors, power systems, and board-level behaviour.
* Strong practical judgment: you can move quickly, but you know when reliability, testability, and process matter. You have a good eye for detail.
* Enjoyment of working independently doing broad, hands-on engineering work in a startup or small team.
* Interest in sport, coaching, skiing, or human performance. Beginner skiers welcome.
## Nice to have:
* Experience with Nordic nRF microcontrollers.
* Bluetooth Low Energy experience, especially debugging real-world connection or reliability issues.
* Experience with IMUs, sensor fusion, real-time signal processing, or on-device data processing.
* Experience designing or maintaining automated production test systems.
* Experience with high-volume consumer electronics products.
* PCB layout experience, especially for small, low-power, sensor-rich products.
* Experience with Rust (the language of our server, app and testjig backends).
* Experience building diagnostic tools for customer support, manufacturing, or field debugging.
## Why Join Carv?
* Work on a game-changing product that combines AI, biomechanics, sensors, and coaching.
* Work across the full embedded stack, from electronics and board bring-up through firmware, diagnostics, and production tooling, with broad ownership that lets you shape the product experience end-to-end.
* Help shape the future of digital sports coaching.
* Work with a small, ambitious team where hardware, firmware, software, and product decisions are tightly connected.
* Spend time in the mountains through our Park City and Innsbruck offices, and work with some of the best ski professionals in the world.
* Visa sponsorship is available.

The Head of Market Access & Business Intelligence is accountable for the UK market access strategy and execution across Celltrion’s biosimilar portfolio. This role leads all market access activities (national and regional), ensuring optimal patient access and sustainable commercial outcomes through effective engagement with NHS England and commissioning bodies, procurement hubs and trusts, and health policy stakeholders. The post-holder provides leadership and insight across tendering, pricing governance, HTA/NICE guidance, and payer/customer strategy, underpinned by robust business intelligence and compliant stakeholder engagement.
**Accountability:**

* **Access Planning & Stakeholder Engagement:** Lead national and regional access planning, including stakeholder mapping, segmentation and engagement plans for NHS procurement bodies across England and the devolved nations, Integrated Care Boards (ICBs), health boards, provider trusts, procurement hubs and key influencers.
* **Policy Influence & External Engagement:** Monitor, interpret and help shape the UK policy and reimbursement environment through engagement with the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC), NHS England and relevant stakeholders; represent the organisation in key industry forums including the British Biosimilars Association (BBA), Medicines UK and ABPI working groups, and coordinate engagement with MHRA on biosimilar-specific considerations in partnership with the Responsible Person/QA & Regulatory Affairs teams.
* **Competitor Intelligence & Strategic Foresight**: Lead systematic competitor intelligence on price positioning and forward-looking policy landscaping, including analysis of Voluntary Scheme for Branded Medicines Pricing and Access (VPAG) and related frameworks, to anticipate market shifts, identify risks and opportunities, and enable proactive, strategically agile decision-making.
* **NHS Partnerships & Access Enablement**: Build and maintain strategic partnerships with NHS procurement and commissioning stakeholders (including NHS England and CMU/procurement leads), leading biosimilar-specific access initiatives such as switching frameworks, pathway optimisation, and service redesign and implementation resources in collaboration with Medical and system partners.
* **Tendering, Contracting & Pricing Governance**: Be accountable for tender and contracting outcomes across the UK (NHS and, where applicable, private markets), including ownership of tender pipeline governance, bid/no-bid decisions, pricing governance, scenario planning and senior escalation management, to deliver sustainable revenue, margin and access.
* **Commercial Integration & Field Enablement**: Provide market access leadership to commercial account teams (RBMs/KAMs), ensuring consistent, compliant and up-to-date value messaging to support biosimilar adoption and switching programmes.
* **Cross-functional Alignment & Execution****:** Partner cross-functionally with Medical, Regulatory Affairs/QA (Responsible Person), Marketing, Supply/Operations and Finance to ensure access strategy, evidence generation and supply plans are aligned and executable.
* **Performance Management & Insight Generation****:** Establish clear governance, reporting and cadence for market access performance (tenders, uptake, share, pricing and guideline alignment), including NICE horizon scanning and implementation tracking; provide regular insights and recommendations to UK leadership.
* **Leadership & Organisational Capability:** Lead, develop and integrate a multidisciplinary team spanning NHS Collaboration, Business Intelligence (Business Excellence, SFE), and Contracts & Tenders; drive high performance, clear accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement, while informing resource allocation to support departmental growth.

**Key Responsibilities****:**
**Strategic Leadership & Market Access Planning**

* **Commissioning & Payer Engagement**: Drive commissioning and payer engagement, working closely with NHS England, ICBs, procurement hubs and provider trusts to support access, uptake and switching in line with local governance and best practice.
* **NICE & Evidence Strategy**: Lead NICE responsibilities end-to-end: horizon scan and assess relevant NICE work programmes (e.g., Technology Appraisals, Highly Specialised Technologies and clinical guidelines); develop internal evidence/value strategies with Medical and HEOR; coordinate any company input to scoping and consultations; lead planning for submissions (where applicable) and responses to requests for information; and translate published guidance into actionable UK implementation plans (formulary, commissioning and pathway implications), including field/brand enablement.
* **Market Intelligence & Competitive Insight**: Maintain deep understanding of the UK biosimilars landscape, including competitor activity, policy developments, commissioning trends and clinical practice changes; translate insights into opportunities and risk mitigation plans.
**Launch, Access Execution & Commercial Operations**
* **Product Readiness & Market Entry Execution**: Lead UK market access operational requirements for successful product launch, including securing PIP codes, managing list price submissions and approvals, ensuring timely inclusion in relevant NHS and commercial pricing databases (e.g. dm+d), and coordinating pre-tender access enablers such as formulary submissions, reimbursement pathway alignment, supply readiness, and compliance with procurement requirements.
* **Tendering, Contracting & Pricing Governance**: Own tendering and contracting excellence across the biosimilars portfolio; set strategy across NHS Commissioning Frameworks and other procurement routes, define bid/no-bid and pricing guardrails, and lead cross-functional governance through to approval. Oversee submission quality and timelines delivered by the Tenders & Contracts Associate, ensuring robust documentation, compliance and audit readiness; lead senior engagement and escalation with NHS procurement and commissioning stakeholders during tender cycles; and drive continuous improvement through win/loss reviews, contract performance monitoring and risk mitigation, including supply continuity considerations.
* **Private Contracting & Commercial Governance**: Lead contracting strategy beyond NHS frameworks, including oversight of private healthcare contracting priorities and negotiation approach; partner with Finance/Legal (as applicable) to manage commercial, governance and compliance risks and ensure contracts align with company policies.
* **Biosimilar Adoption & Pathway Support**: Provide biosimilar pathway leadership, developing materials and support for switching/adoption initiatives with Medical, and ensuring external activities remain compliant and appropriately certified.
**External Affairs, Governance & Cross-functional Leadership**
* **External Affairs & Industry Engagement**: Build and maintain relationships with key governance and industry bodies, including the British Biosimilars Association (BBA), ABPI and relevant working groups, ensuring Celltrion’s participation is proactive, coordinated and compliant.
* **Regulatory & Safety Pathway Support**: In partnership with QA/Regulatory Affairs (Responsible Person), take the lead in supporting biosimilar-specific regulatory and safety pathway considerations, including coordination of MHRA-related topics that impact access, supply or stakeholder communications.
* **Cross-functional Governance & Alignment**: Lead cross-functional market access governance with Medical, Marketing, Supply/Operations and Finance to ensure strategic alignment, continuity of supply, contracting readiness and consistent external messaging.
* **Representation & Internal Enablement**: Represent Celltrion at relevant external meetings and forums (including PDIG where applicable) and ensure internal teams are briefed and enabled on outcomes, actions and compliance considerations.
* **Compliance & SOP Adherence**: Ensure all activities comply with ABPI Code of Practice, PMCPA guidance and internal SOPs, including governance of materials and interactions with external stakeholders.
**Performance, Insights & Team Leadership**
* **Leadership Reporting & Risk Management**: Provide regular updates to UK leadership on tender pipeline, contract performance, access barriers/risks and policy changes, with clear recommendations and mitigations.
* **Business Intelligence & Insights**: Lead the Business Intelligence capability; line manage the Business Intelligence Analyst and ensure timely, accurate insights (market, tender, competitor, pricing and performance) via agreed dashboards and reports to support decision-making.
* **People Leadership & Team Development**: Line manage the Tenders & Contracts Associate and the NHS & Collaborations lead/direct report, setting clear objectives, developing capability and ensuring robust cross-team ways of working.

* Significant experience in UK pharmaceuticals/biologics, with strong UK market access responsibility, including tendering, contracting and NHS commissioning.
* Strong understanding of the UK biosimilars market, including procurement environments, access drivers, pricing governance and policy or regulatory considerations.
* Proven ability to engage and influence senior stakeholders across NHS England, ICBs, trusts, procurement bodies and relevant external organisations.
* Experience working with, and/or representing a company through, relevant industry bodies (e.g., BBA, ABPI) and understanding of the UK regulatory landscape (including MHRA) in collaboration with QA/Regulatory.

Production data modelling: Translate analyst requirements and SQL into robust, production-grade dbt models (source → warehouse → reporting layers). You'll own data contracts, documentation, testing, and scheduling, with orchestration managed via Prefect.

Real dbt experience: You've built and maintained models in a genuine project - incremental logic, tests, an understanding of why downstream consumers matter. It doesn't need to have been enormous; it needs to have been real. BigQuery experience is a plus; another warehouse is fine.
Solid Python and SQL skills, with the instinct that code going to production deserves tests.
Practical AWS Experience: You have hands-on experience deploying and debugging in AWS. You don't need to know every service we use on day one - we’ll teach you our specific stack.

Collaborative Communication: You can sit side-by-side with analysts, understand the intent behind their SQL, and partner with them to translate complex business logic into efficient, production-ready solutions.

Vacancy Information We have a vacancy for an Assistant Psychologist to administer and score psychometric assessments that contribute to wider psychological assessments of parents and children undertaken as part of expert witness work for the family court. The post-holder may also contribute to our services related to screening the psychological adjustment of young people in children's residential homes, or working with local authorities. We expect that the majority of the work will be located around Coventry, Birmingham and east Cheshire, but it may involve travel further afield for two or three days per month. This role involves travelling to various locations in the area and gathering information, setting up meetings, administering psychometric assessments and contributing to reports and letters. We have 6 months of funding initially, whilst another AP in the team is seconded into a project funded by a grant, so we are initially recruiting to a fixed term contract. However, we have other grant applications submitted through the BERRI side of the business, for which we will hear the results in January. If any of these are successful, that could lead to this post being extended. Likewise, we have several members of staff who have applied for clinical training this year, and again, this could create longer-term vacancies if any of them secure a place. The contract of employment will be with LifePsychol Ltd, and you are likely to have a mixture of working from home, out in the field and our offices in Sutton Coldfield. This role cannot be done remotely, and we expect the postholder to be fully immunised and willing to engage positively with applicable precautions to prevent the spread of covid-19, such as wearing masks or social distancing, where applicable, and sanitising materials between uses. The post involves a combination of: - summarising legal bundles - administering psychometric assessments - writing up reports to a template provided - gathering background information from files - collecting questionnaire data from schools and parents/foster parents/residential care staff - gathering outcome data and using an online outcome measurement tool (see BERRI.org.uk) - acting as a champion for the outcome measurement protocol within services - providing summary reports from outcome data/questionnaires - making structured observations of children - gathering third party observational data It may also involve - data entry and statistical analysis - writing literature reviews - contributing to academic papers for publication - general administrative tasks (arranging meetings, responding to telephone and email enquiries, keeping track of materials, etc) - other such tasks as the business requires You'll be part of a small local team, co-located with a qualified clinical psychologist, and remotely linked into a wider national team that includes a consultant clinical psychologist, two other clinical psychologists, 3 other AP/psych graduates, various students on placement, and a wider operations, sales and admin team. We also fund a research team at the Anna Freud Centre / UCL. This means there are lots of interesting people within the network to learn from. There will be opportunities to sit in on training events, and you may be able to contribute to research and publications. The nature of the roles this post will undertake means that we require a psychology graduate with GBC (at a 2:1 or better, or with a completed post-graduate qualification), who has a driving license and access to a vehicle (or can propose suitable adaptation if they have a disability that prevents this). We need someone who is proactive, diligent and meticulous about collecting and writing up information. Experience administering psychometric assessments would be advantageous but is not essential, as full training will be provided. You need to be organised and persistent, able to set up meetings and communicate in a professional manner, including writing up reports to a high standard. Fluency with computer and internet applications is also necessary. We want you to share our mission to improve the lives of people who have experienced adversity. You need to have the kind of personality and resilience required to be part of a team that makes a difference for some of the most complex and vulnerable children in the country. We are a supportive team and positive about diversity. We like to give you the opportunity to show us what you are capable of, and we see our staff as our most valuable resource. We provide regular supervision, and plenty of opportunities for personal development. Supervision will be provided by a qualified clinical psychologist. We have a commitment to training and development, and a good track record of past assistants gaining places on clinical training (though I suspect this is as much about who I select as the experiences we provide). We are a real living wage employer. The salary for this post is £21,225 per annum. We reimburse the cost of travel undertaken to fulfil this role (from your home or base office, according to which is nearer). We also provide a health scheme to cover the costs of eye tests and dental check-ups and reimburse some of the costs of other health treatments, as well as other benefits such as access to counselling, GP services and an advice line. How to apply **If you want to apply for this position then please send a CV (no longer than 2 pages) and a brief covering letter/expression of interest (no more than 600 words) here explaining how you are suited to the position. We do not consider applications that do not have a covering letter explaining how your skills match our requirements.** Please also include the telephone/email contact details for two references. Please apply as soon as possible. We expect to close applications at midnight on Sunday 27th November, but may close earlier if we have sufficient applicants of suitable calibre. We hope to interview over zoom on Wednesday 7th December. The post is funded for six months from 3rd January. Background information LifePsychol/BERRI/Evolving Families are a set of small clinical psychology companies that have particular expertise about children and families, particularly when it comes to attachment, parenting and recovery from adversity. Our main specialist area is around attachment, trauma and maltreatment and how this evidence base can inform the care of children who do not live in their family of origin. The tools that we have developed help local authorities, placement providers and parents/carers to identify, support and advocate for the psychological needs of their child. We use specialist psychological expertise to undertake assessments for the family courts, as well as for the local authorities and placement providers that we work with. In addition, we run a neurodevelopmental assessment clinic, that helps to identify autism, learning disability and other neurodiverse conditions, which is based in Sutton Coldfield. The company is small but growing rapidly. Our mission is to improve outcomes for children with complex needs. Our aim is to change the way that children's psychological needs are looked at in the UK (and then around the world), by identifying psychological needs that encompass behaviour, relationships, development, risk and a broad range of indicators of wellbeing. Through identifying needs better, and tracking how they change over time we want to improve the quality of placements and services for children, starting with those who are in the Care system. We hope to achieve this ambitious goal through structured needs assessments and regular use of outcome measures. We then hope to spread this methodology to other groups of children with complex needs, such as those at the edge of care, or in specialist educational provision, those who have experienced adversity, and children with psychological needs that are hard to meet with traditional services due to the pandemic. We hope to see our system used in every local authority, placement provider, school and charity that provides children's services to inform the way that psychological needs are identified and addressed. The assessments we undertake and the training, pathway and standards we help services to implement are about ensuring that children's needs are identified and the strategies carers use are effective, evidence-based, individualised to the background and context of each child, and evolve as the child’s needs change. Our care plans are based on a thorough psychological assessment and a multi-faceted formulation of the child’s needs. We have developed a set of online tools for parents, carers, professionals, commissioners and placement providers to use to identify and track the psychological needs of children. We call it the BERRI system, because our tools explore Behaviour, Emotional well-being, Risk to self and others, Relationships and Indicators of conditions that need to be understood to care effectively for the child. BERRI allows us to gain a more holistic picture of children’s needs, to track how this changes over time and to target particular concerns and monitor the effectiveness of interventions to address them. Our initial data suggests that we can help to ensure that children's psychological needs are effectively identified and addressed, improving their outcomes whilst we save costs to the public purse. Our services gain exceptional feedback from carers and professionals, but we hold ourselves to tough standards of evidence, and gather data about our effectiveness every step of the way.

Experience administering psychometric assessments would be advantageous but is not essential, as full training will be provided. You need to be organised and proactive, able to set up meetings and communicate in a professional manner, including writing up reports to a high standard. Fluency with computer and internet applications is also necessary. We want you to share our mission to improve the lives of young people who have experienced adversity (and we would see lived experience of adversity or care experience as a strength). You need to have the kind of personality and resilience required to be part of a team that makes a difference for some of the most complex children in the country. We like to give you the opportunity to show us what you are capable of, and we see our staff as our most valuable resource. We provide supervision according to BPS recommendations, and plenty of opportunities for personal development. Supervision will be provided by a qualified clinical psychologist. We have a commitment to training and development, and a good track record of past assistants gaining places on clinical training (though I suspect this is as much about who I select as the experiences we provide). Salary is based on a full time rate of £23,302 per annum (we are proud to be a living wage employer), but will be paid pro rata if you opt to take a lower number of hours. **- How to apply -** **If you want to apply for this position then please send a CV (no longer than 2 pages) and a brief covering letter/expression of interest (no more than 600 words) through this website [link to be added shortly] explaining how you are suited to the position.** We only consider applications that include the covering letter. You must also include the telephone/email contact details for two references. Please apply as soon as possible. We expect to close applications at midnight on Sunday 13th August, but may close earlier if we have sufficient applicants of suitable calibre. We hope to interview on Weds 30th August. Background information: BERRI is an award-winning clinical psychology company that has particular expertise about children and families, particularly when it comes to attachment, parenting and recovery from adversity. Our main specialist area is around attachment, trauma and maltreatment and how this evidence base can inform the care of children who do not live in their family of origin. We therefore provide training for adoptive, foster and residential carers, as well as health, social care and legal professionals. The company is small but growing rapidly. Our mission is to improve outcomes for children with complex needs. Our aim is to change the way that children's psychological needs are looked at in the UK (and then around the world), by identifying both mental health symptoms and needs that are outside the traditional medical model and encompass behaviour, relationships, development, risk and a broad range of indicators of wellbeing. Through identifying needs better, and tracking how they change over time we want to improve the quality of placements and services for children, starting with those who are in the Care system. We hope to achieve this ambitious goal by training carers, implementing a new set of standards for care providers, and through structured needs assessments and regular use of outcome measures (BERRI). We then hope to spread this methodology to other groups of children with complex needs, such as those at the edge of care, or in specialist educational provision, poor school attenders or those who have experienced adversity. We hope to see our system used in every local authority, placement provider, school and charity that provides children's services to inform the way that psychological needs are identified and addressed. Why start with children who are in Care? Children in Care are a particularly vulnerable group of children and young people because their needs are complex and they have experienced multiple adversities that put them at greater risk of negative outcomes. Local Authorities are spending £9 billion on children's social care, including £3 billion on placements every year, but there is little evidence about what works to improve life chances and reduce risks because very little data is being collected. We want to change this, and to ensure that the systems around children are psychologically minded and informed by the latest evidence. The training, pathway and standards we implement are about ensuring that strategies carers use are evidence-based, individualised to the background and needs of each child, evolve as the child’s needs change, and are based on a thorough psychological assessment and a multi-faceted formulation of the child’s needs. We believe that having advice from a clinical psychologist to inform the care of all Children in and on the edge of Care (and other children with complex needs) will both reduce stigma and improve outcomes, whilst helping carers to feel better equipped to meet the children’s needs. We have developed a training program and care pathway as one means to implement these standards for placements. We have also developed a set of online tools for commissioners and placement providers to use to identify and track the needs of children in their care. The tools are known by the acronym ‘BERRI’ because they explore Behaviour, Emotional well-being, Risk to self and others, Relationships and Indicators of conditions that need to be understood to care effectively for the child. We want every young person with complex needs to have a service that meets their needs in an effective and evidence-based way. We have therefore developed tools that allow us to gain a more holistic picture of children’s needs, to track how this changes over time and to target particular concerns and monitor the effectiveness of interventions to address them. Our data suggests that we can help to ensure that children's psychological needs are effectively identified and addressed. Our pilots have shown we can reduce children's needs significantly using the pathway and tools we provide, and save costs to the public purse whilst we do so. Our services gain exceptional feedback from carers and professionals, but we hold ourselves to tough standards of evidence, and gather data about our effectiveness every step of the way.

You will translate divisional supply chain strategy into clear, practical plans that support customer service, cost efficiency, inventory optimisation, risk management, and operational resilience.

You will lead, coach, and develop a team of site-based Supply Chain Managers, creating a stronger, more consistent planning community across the division.

### **Why this matters**
To meet global demand, the world needs to mine as much copper in the next 25 years as in all of human history. Today's methods cannot scale to this challenge. We are developing frontier technology to fix this, starting with the core of every mining company: the understanding of the orebody.
We're a Cambridge University spin-out using explainable AI and value-of-information analysis to transform how mines are developed and operated. Our uncertainty-aware models map subsurface resources from multimodal data, so mining companies can make faster evidence-based decisions on where to drill next and how best to move sites forward. * **Turn models into decisions.** The ML team hands you probabilistic block-model outputs and drill planning optimisation options. The geologist hands you a client’s requirements. You shape the model into an output that's right for this deposit and ready for a geologist to explain to the client.
* **Benchmark against the standards.** You benchmark our approach head-to-head against the methods clients already use (e.g. ordinary and indicator kriging, conditional simulation) so we can communicate the exact benefits and honest trade-offs.
* **Build the foundation, not the notebook.** You leave behind reusable, tested workflows the next deposit inherits, not a one-off script only you can run.

We combine drillhole data, structural interpretation, geophysics and geochemical data to give teams across that span a faster, more reliable quantification of the properties of their deposit.

OverviewApplication
Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout. We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.
As a **Senior Technical Account Manager,** you will serve as a critical strategic partner and trusted technical advisor for our most complex and high-value customers. You will accelerate customer outcomes, ensure their success with the Docker platform and architect their long-term transformation strategies in partnership with their leadership. You'll be a Docker expert who shapes the future of their technical success and who translates their business goals into impactful, long-term technical success plans.
# **Responsibilities**
* Lead the strategic vision for multiple high-value enterprise accounts, driving adoption and expansion by aligning Docker's capabilities with their long-term business objectives.
* Act as the voice of the customer for the product and engineering teams, synthesising and prioritising feedback from multiple accounts to directly influence the Docker product roadmap.
* ​Conduct platform health assessments and maturity reviews, delivering best practices across Dockerfiles, images, CI/CD, registry strategy, and secure software supply chain governance.
* ​Guide customers on AI-assisted development workflows and operational governance, connecting Docker's AI capabilities to their broader platform strategy.
* Architect and execute complex adoption plans that address critical technical and business challenges.
* Lead and facilitate Strategic Business Reviews, presenting a comprehensive view of the customer's technical journey and demonstrating the strategic value and ROI of their partnership with Docker to senior leadership.
# **Qualifications**
* 4+ years of experience in a customer-facing technical role (e.g., Senior TAM, Principal Solutions Architect, Solution Engineer or DevOps Consultant), with a demonstrated track record of managing and expanding high-value enterprise accounts.
* Deep, hands-on expertise in containerization, CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, and the broader cloud-native ecosystem.
* Proven ability to lead and orchestrate technical strategy for multiple, complex accounts, proactively identifying and resolving systemic issues before they become critical.
* Exceptional executive presence and communication skills, with a track record of building trusted relationships with C-level and VP-level stakeholders.
* Bonus: Experience building or contributing to a formal TAM program.
# **What to Expect**
## **First 30 Days**
* Complete onboarding and ramp-up training on Docker’s products, tools, and engagement frameworks.
* Shadow experienced TAMs and Solution Engineers on customer calls to learn engagement rhythms.
* Meet your portfolio of customers and understand their environments, goals, and success metrics.
* Build relationships with internal partners including Support, Product, and Sales.
* Review existing customer documentation and success plans to identify initial opportunities for impact.
## **First 90 Days**
* Take ownership of a customer portfolio and begin leading account engagements. Conduct your first technical or executive business reviews with guidance from your manager.
* Establish a cadence of customer check-ins, documenting key success milestones and adoption progress.
* Identify at least one process or content improvement that can scale customer engagement or reduce friction.
* Contribute to cross-functional discussions that connect customer insights with product feedback.
## **One-year Outlook**
* Own the full lifecycle for a portfolio of strategic or enterprise customers, delivering measurable improvements in adoption and health scores.
* Build executive relationships and serve as the customer’s voice within Docker.
* Contribute to building the broader TAM engagement model through shared best practices and enablement resources.
* Demonstrate impact through increased customer value realization, renewal success, and platform expansion.
* Mentor new TAMs and participate in developing scalable frameworks for onboarding and customer engagement.
